name: romantic love
quote: The old couple held hands on the beach.
description: A deep sense that another person is the best choice to fulfill multiple long term needs and that you are theirs.

variations.name: crush
variations.description: A perception that your person of interest is so attractive and wonderful that you'd like to be associated with them.
examples: She has a poster of that boy band.

variations.name: new love
variations.description: The first part of a mutually romantic relationship where rewarding brain chemicals are plentiful.

variations.name: codependent love
variations.description: A couple that has lost enough of their independent identities such that minor relationship stress becomes major.
examples: They can't bear to be apart for even a day.

variations.name: lustful love
variations.description: When perception of 'true love' are mostly a deception, perhaps even self-deception, covering a drive for sex and/or social credit.

variations.name: isolated love
variations.description: A perception that the other person is the best choice to fulfill your long term needs, but they don't even know you. This is more than a crush and can range from innocent to unhealthy.

variations.name: one-sided love
variations.description: A perception that the other person the best choice to fulfill your long term needs, but although they know you, they don't reciprocate this feeling. This could be a previous relationsip or someone just not interested.
examples: He missed her dearly after she broke up with him.

commentaries.quote: Valentine-style romantic love may be fun, but mostly that's from brain chemicals reacting to the promise of short-term physical and social rewards. Underlying the whole froth, though, is something pretty powerful - we humans have a deep desire to pair bond.

The outer behaviors of pair bonding can look different across cultures. The inner experience of it is appealing to many for some good reasons: the brain may like the stability, the culture may encourage it, and it may help reproductive success.
Yes, love and the search for it can be a social mess. But we keep at it, we sing about it, we talk about it, we structure our lives around it. There's something there.

Your mate can help fulfill important needs: companionship, sex, co-parenting, validation, and a sense of existential completion. But it might make sense to not depend on one person for everything all the time.

This study on Hadza people may shed new light on the meaning of love in humans' hunter-gatherer past, in which individuals, not their parents, were responsible for partner choice. We hypothesize that passion and commitment were among the key factors increasing reproductive success.
commentaries.attribution: paraphrased from 'Love Influences Reproductive Success in Humans' Piotr Sorokowski, et. al. Frontiers in Psychology, 20 November 2017

commentaries.quote: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud. It does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs.

conditions: Deep perception that another person is the best choice to fulfill mulitple long term needs and that you are theirs.
